anomaly_def.Name: Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly + Buffer Cache and Latch Contention Anomaly + CPU Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly: Engine-level settings (memory pools, checkpoint cadence, parallelism, etc.) are mis-tuned relative to hardware capacity and workload characteristics.
Buffer Cache and Latch Contention Anomaly: Sessions serialize on hot buffer pages, latches, or I/O slots, causing page-level stalls regardless of total memory size.
CPU Resource Anomaly: Database processes collectively saturate host CPU, driving high run-queue pressure and system-wide latency.

When all three root causes co-exist, the system exhibits a multifaceted bottleneck pattern: CPU utilization hovers at or near 100 %, yet throughput stays flat because many runnable threads spin or block on buffer-busy and latch waits. Wait-event views report an alternating mix of latch, buffer-busy, and scheduler/run-queue waits; OS metrics show high context-switch and spin time with pockets of idle I/O capacity. Checkpoint storms or aggressive background writers triggered by mis-set parameters extend the dirty-page queue, prolonging latch hold times and further bloating CPU usage. End-user queries suffer from unpredictable latency spikes and throughput collapse that do not improve even when more CPU cores are provisioned or when isolated configuration knobs are tweaked.

Causally, ill-chosen configuration parameters (e.g., undersized buffer pool, overly aggressive checkpoint interval, excessive worker or parallelism limits) create hot pages and rapid buffer churn, which magnify latch contention inside the buffer manager. The same mis-configuration often spawns too many runnable workers; as they fight for the same latches, they spin, driving up CPU consumption and inflating the run queue. Elevated CPU pressure in turn lengthens the time to service background flushes and checkpoints, keeping dirty pages in memory longer and re-intensifying latch contention—a feedback loop that obscures the original mis-configuration and makes the combined anomaly more severe than any single root cause alone.

entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with a general engine-level execution problem surfaced by the official error catalogue, but its precise trigger must be interpreted together with workload context and surrounding evidence.
entry.solution_guidance: Review the surrounding workload, official description, and engine state to determine whether the issue is rooted in SQL logic, resource pressure, configuration, or environmental instability.
